intro.TrustedMarkup: Orders, the comparison under one, and the functions that sort by one. Asc, Desc, Then, Elem, Order and before are compiler-known: an order is a type, never a value, and only these three make one. The ascending order of T: by each named field in turn, or by T's own value with no field. Asc<Person, age> orders people by age. A key is an integer, a Bool or a String; Strings compare bytewise.

prose.TrustedMarkup: The ascending order of T: by each named field in turn, or by T's own value with no field. Asc<Person, age> orders people by age. A key is an integer, a Bool or a String; Strings compare bytewise.
The order A, then B among the values A ties. A and B order one type.
The type the order O compares: Elem<Asc<Person, age>> is Person.
The bound of a type parameter that stands for an order. Asc, Desc and Then satisfy it, and nothing else does.

sig.TrustedMarkup: fn before<O: Order>(a: Elem<O>, b: Elem<O>) -> Bool

prose.TrustedMarkup: Whether a is strictly before b under O. Two values tie under O when neither is before the other.

sig.TrustedMarkup: fn sort<O: Order>(xs: consume Array<Elem<O>>) -> Array<Elem<O>> where sorted<O>(value)

prose.TrustedMarkup: xs sorted by O, stably: values that tie keep their order. An insertion sort, quadratic in the length.

sig.TrustedMarkup: fn insertSorted<O: Order>( xs: consume Array<Elem<O>> where sorted<O>(value), v: consume Elem<O>, ) -> Array<Elem<O>> where sorted<O>(value)

prose.TrustedMarkup: The sorted xs with v inserted after every value it is not before.

sig.TrustedMarkup: fn mergeSorted<O: Order>( a: consume Array<Elem<O>> where sorted<O>(value), b: consume Array<Elem<O>> where sorted<O>(value), ) -> Array<Elem<O>> where sorted<O>(value)

prose.TrustedMarkup: The sorted a and b as one sorted array. Of two values that tie, a's comes first.

sig.TrustedMarkup: fn dedupSorted<O: Order>( xs: consume Array<Elem<O>> where sorted<O>(value), ) -> Array<Elem<O>> where strict<O>(value)

prose.TrustedMarkup: The sorted xs with each run of values that tie under O cut to its first.

sig.TrustedMarkup: fn lowerBound<O: Order>( xs: Array<Elem<O>> where sorted<O>(value), v: Elem<O>, ) -> Int64 where value >= 0 && value <= xs.length

prose.TrustedMarkup: The first position in the sorted xs whose value v is not after: the count of values before v. Binary search.
